# DunJS Changelog

Historical record of phased deliveries. Newest at the bottom.
Production blockers list is empty as of v0.4.0; design-level
won't-fix items moved into [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) `## Won't-fix
design constraints`.

| 28b | fs binary write/read | `fs.writeFileSync` / `appendFileSync` / `writeFile` / `appendFile` (promises) / `readFile` (promises) were UTF-8-coding Buffer / Uint8Array payloads (every byte >= 0x80 → 3-byte U+FFFD replacement). Real Node writes raw bytes. Fixed across all 5 entry points; readFile-promises returns a Buffer when no encoding is given. New `fs_binary.js` fixture: 9/9 across QJS/JSC/V8 | **Done** |
| 28c | DIP1000 audit | `return scope` annotations on `IJSEngine.getTypedArrayBytes` + the 3 backend overrides + `dun.builtins.buffer.extractBytes`. Slice-lifetime contract is now machine-checked through virtual dispatch (DIP1000 doesn't infer `scope` for virtuals). Documented active `-preview=` flags + DIP refs in CLAUDE.md | **Done** |
| 28d | GC config sweep | Profiled `feature_bench` across 6 GC configs × 3 backends. Default `minPoolSize:16` is at the throughput knee; `:32` halves GCs but throughput is noise-equal, `:64` regresses JSC 10%, `parallel:4` no-op for single-threaded JS, `gc:precise` no-op for this workload. CLAUDE.md table updated with measured numbers | **Done** |
| 29a | DIP1038 `@mustuse` JSResult | `core.attribute.mustuse` on `JSResult` forces every `engine.eval(...)` caller to either inspect `isError` or hand the value to a consumer; compiler immediately surfaced 2 latent bugs in worker init code where eval results were silently dropped (Worker installer, `__filename`/`__dirname` setup) — if the inline JS ever failed the worker would crash later with `Worker is undefined` and no stderr diagnostic | **Done** |
| 29b | DIP1038 `@mustuse` AsyncResult | Same annotation on `AsyncResult` (`dun.loop.async`) — every async worker delegate must build via `AsyncResult.ok(...)` / `.fail(...)` and return it. Defensive: no violations found in tree, but locks the contract going forward | **Done** |
| 29c | `mustEval` helper | `dun.engine.iface.mustEval(engine, source, filename, what)` — canonical drop-only consumer for the `@mustuse JSResult`. Asserts non-error, frees the value. Two call sites converted (`worker_api.installWorkerAPI` Worker installer, `workers.worker._runWorker` `__filename`/`__dirname` setup). Future closed-world eval init code should reach for this instead of duplicating the assert+freeValue pattern | **Done** |

| 31n | Lazy-getter trick (JSC GC unblock) | Eager install of the last 12 web extras (observers, WebTransport, WebRTC, IndexedDB, Notification, CookieStore, FileReaderSync, ImageBitmap) deadlocks JSC's concurrent GC: the collector thread suspends D worker threads to walk stacks, but the D event-loop thread is already in `nanosleep` waiting for I/O. `deno_deploy_compat` failed deterministically 6/7 with `f30ac7a`. `gdb` confirmed the cycle (`WTF::Thread::suspend` blocked on semaphore vs. `dun.loop.eventloop.EventLoop.tick` in `nanosleep`). Fix: each chunk becomes a tag + per-global `Object.defineProperty` getter. First access deletes every accessor the chunk owns (so the chunk's `if (typeof X === 'undefined')` checks see a clean state), then `new Function(src)()`s the body. Subsequent reads hit data properties. Same pattern Deno itself uses in `libs/core/01_core.js` (`propNonEnumerableLazyLoaded` + `createLazyLoader`) — verified by walking the Deno clone. Zero install-time JS allocation for the 12 extras; JSC collector never sees the trigger pressure | **Done** |

| 36a | net.d / ws.d slot recycling | Per `/debug-native-callback` skill's "Slot exhaustion" fix pattern. Close paths push the slot id back. Prevents monotonic growth of `sockets[]` / `wsConns[]` arrays under long-running services accepting many connections | **Done** |
| 36b | ThreadSanitizer audit + worker.d race fix | Built with `dub build -b tsan` (existing config) and ran the workers fixture. TSan caught a real data race: `WorkerState.status_` was written from the worker thread (lines 109, 112 in spawnWorker's delegate) without holding `gWorkersMutex`, while the main thread read it under the mutex. Fix: replaced direct field access with `loadStatus` / `storeStatus` helpers that use `core.atomic.atomicLoad/Store` with acq/rel barriers. The mutex stays for the gWorkers array walk; the per-worker status is now lockfree. TSan now reports zero races (only a benign "thread leak" for daemonized worker threads, which is by design) | **Done** |
| 36c | shared_memory.d: lockfree refcount | SharedArrayBuffer registry's `sabRef` / `sabUnref` previously took the registry mutex for a single int increment. Hot path for cross-worker shared state. Refactored: `refCount` is now `shared int` with `atomicOp!"+="` for ref / atomicOp `-=` for unref. `sabAlloc` keeps the mutex (array growth is rare). `sabUnref` takes the mutex only when the refcount drops to zero (free + clear ptr) — also rare. Net: zero mutex acquisitions on the hot ref/unref path for live SABs | **Done** |

| 38a | **CVE-class path-traversal fix** | `Permission.check(read/write/run/ffi, resource)` was comparing the raw user-supplied path against the scope via `startsWith` + boundary check, so `/tmp/safe/../../etc/hostname` matched a scope of `/tmp/safe` (literal prefix match) but the OS opened `/etc/hostname`. Same class as Node's CVE-2023-32004 (fs.lutimes), CVE-2024-21896 (path traversal in fs in worker), and several Deno permission-bypass advisories. Fix: canonicalize the resource via `dun.platform.paths.canonicalizePath` (which uses `buildNormalizedPath(absolutePath(...))`) BEFORE scope matching. Also canonicalize the scope patterns in `grantScoped` / `denyScoped` so a `--allow-read=./safe` scope matches absolute resources after the resource normalization. New `cve_path_traversal.js` fixture — 5/5 across QJS / JSC / V8 (legit reads still succeed; `..` traversal blocked; nested traversal blocked; absolute-outside blocked; relative `.` scope still works) | **Done** |

| 39a | Bun perf port: drop redundant `.idup` clones | Mirroring upstream Bun's "drop redundant clone()" / "borrow instead of to_vec" pattern (commits 174a2c99, 654d2d9d, c9c9eab5 and similar in the v1.x.x clone-tracer pass). Hot-path call sites that did `engine.newString(X.idup)` were double-copying: `newString` takes `scope const(char)[]` and copies into engine-owned storage itself. Removed across 9 modules: net.d (per-read TCP), buffer.d (Buffer.toString utf8), tls.d (per-read TLS), ws.d (frame.payload), os.d (hostname/release/userInfo/machine — 6 sites), dgram.d (address strings — 2 sites), sqlite.d (libversion + column_text), fs.d (realpathSync — `.idup` between fromStringz and free reordered to `newString` first then free), fs_promises.d (dirent name + readdir entries). Crypto cipher/decipher/hmac/dh `toHexString!(LetterCase.lower)(X).idup` triple-allocations also removed in the same pass (see 39b) | **Done** |
| 39b | Crypto: SIMD `hexEncode` for digest hot paths | Added `hexEncode(const(ubyte)[])` and `hexEncodeFixed!N(const ubyte[N])` to `dun.platform.simd`. The dynamic-size variant does one GC allocation + the existing SIMD 16-byte/cycle interleave path (LDC: `shufflevector`); the CTFE-sized variant stack-allocates `char[2*N]` so callers with known sizes (GCM auth tag = 16 bytes) skip the GC entirely. Migrated 9 crypto hot paths from `std.digest`'s serial `toHexString` to SIMD: cipher.update/final, decipher.update/final, encodeOutput (HMAC/digest), DH computeSecret, BN→hex. GCM `_authTag` now uses `hexEncodeFixed!16` (stack-only). The unused `toHexString` import at the digest fallback switch was also dropped | **Done** |
| 39c | HTTP request-line splitter: SIMD `findByte` | `parseRequestHeaders` previously scanned the request buffer one byte at a time looking for `'\n'`, `' '`, and `':'`. Switched all four scans to `dun.platform.simd.findByte`, which jumps 16 bytes/cycle on LDC (via `llvm_cttz` movemask-equivalent). Each HTTP request used to touch every byte of the header block; now it touches 1/16th. Same parser logic — request line splits, header name lowercasing (still uses `asciiToLowerBuf`), and header interning are unchanged | **Done** |

| 40a | StackFallback arena primitive | Mirrors Bun's `std.heap.stackFallback(N, default_allocator)` pattern used across `node_assert_binding.zig`, `node_os.zig`, `node_process.zig`, etc. for per-call scratch buffers. New `StackFallback!N` struct in `dun.platform.arena`: pairs `InSituRegion!N` (stack) with GC `new[]` overflow so callers don't have to bookkeep heap-spilled blocks (the GC reclaims them when references drop). `deallocateAll()` resets the stack region; GC blocks fall out of scope naturally. Unit-tested (allocate-within-budget + overflow-to-heap paths) | **Done** |
| 40b | `Buffer.toString('latin1')` adopts StackFallback | First production user of `StackFallback!2048`. The latin1 path needs a scratch `char[]` only to pass to `newString` (which copies into engine storage). For the bulk of latin1 decodes (≤2KB — typical Buffer-to-string conversion sizes), the scratch buffer lives entirely on the stack with zero GC pressure; larger buffers spill silently. Mirrors upstream Bun's `node_process.zig` `stack_fallback_allocator` pattern at line 153 | **Done** |

Integration grid: **146/146** on QJS / V8, **145/145 + 1 SKIP** on JSC. Foundation for further arena-pattern ports as future hot paths are identified | **Done** |
| 41a | `Buffer.toString('latin1')` returns correct code points 0x80–0xFF | Audit caught: the latin1 path cast each byte directly to `char` and handed it to `engine.newString` (UTF-8), which silently dropped bytes ≥ 0x80 (invalid 1-byte UTF-8). Fixed by adding `latin1ToUtf8Buf` / `latin1ToUtf8Len` / `latin1ToUtf8MaxLen` to `dun.platform.simd`, encoding each high byte as a 2-byte UTF-8 sequence (0xC2 0x80 .. 0xC3 0xBF). Pre-existing bug exposed by the audit; matches Node / Bun reference behavior on `Buffer.from([0x80, 0xFF]).toString('latin1')` (length 2, code points 0x80 + 0xFF) | **Done** |
| 41b | JSC `newString` is now NUL-safe | Audit caught: JSC's `JSStringCreateWithUTF8CString` is NUL-terminated, so any input containing a 0x00 byte (e.g. `Buffer.from([0x00, 0x7F]).toString('latin1')`) got truncated to 0 bytes. Fixed by adding `JSStringCreateWithCharacters` (length-explicit UTF-16) binding and routing NUL-containing inputs through a UTF-8 → UTF-16 decoder slow path. NUL detection uses `dun.platform.simd.findByte` (SIMD), so the no-NUL fast path stays cheap. All UTF-8 / surrogate constants named (no magic numbers) | **Done** |

Findings: (a) the "CRASH" output in `deno_deploy_compat` is the test's own `Promise.race` timeout caught by its `.catch` — formatted via the `<error-compat>` shim wrapper, not an actual JSC crash; (b) the real bug is a generic JSC HTTP-server-per-cycle handle leak — bisected by replacing `Deno.serve` with `http.createServer` (15+ servers OK), then adding `new Request(url)` per-request to plain http (hangs at 15), confirming the leak is in the JSC server lifecycle, not in v7 extras; (c) v7 extras only shave 7-8 servers off the threshold (17 → 9-10) by adding install-time eval pressure that hits the leak sooner; (d) gdb backtrace at hang shows main thread in `epoll_wait(timeout=0)` watching the listen fd, fetch worker in `read()` on client socket, but `handlerCalled` never fires in the JS handler — the request reaches the server's epoll but never dispatches to JS land. Documented all findings in `bun_extras_v7.d` so the next investigator skips the misleading trails | **Done** |

Added `gHttpPoller.unwatch(ev.fd)` for the unmatched case. Confirmed not the root cause of the JSC SKIP, but the right defensive move | **Done** |

Now both paths protect symmetrically. Doesn't move the JSC SKIP threshold by itself (the deeper leak is elsewhere) but it's a real correctness fix flagged by the audit | **Done** |

| 47a | **JSC cached-handle pin fix (deno_deploy_compat flake gone)** | gdb investigation traced the residual `deno_deploy_compat` flake to JSC's protect-counter underflow on cached `__gshared JSHandle` globals. The pattern was `_cache = engine.dupValue(result.value); engine.freeValue(result.value);` — on JSC, `dupValue` increments the protect counter to 1 and `freeValue` decrements it back to 0, leaving the cached handle unprotected. JSC then collected it under heap pressure, surfacing as `await fetch()` returning `undefined` at the 10-13th sequential server cycle. Fix: double-dup before freeValue (`engine.dupValue(result.value); _cache = engine.dupValue(result.value); engine.freeValue(result.value);`) — the first dup matches the implicit eval ownership the freeValue will drop; the second is the permanent root. Applied to `_fetchResponseBuilder` + `_fetchHeadersFlattener` in `fetch.d`, and `_yamlKeysFn` in `yaml.d` (caught the same pattern proactively). JSC sweep now passes 3/3 standalone — `deno_deploy_compat` no longer flakes under sweep heap-load | **Done** |

| 61a | **ESM/CJS condition order fix in exports resolution** | Discovered while testing `dun install @agentmemory/agentmemory`. The `resolveExportTarget` conditions list was a SINGLE `["dun", "require", "node", "import", "default"]` order used for BOTH `require()` AND `import` contexts. Result: ESM `import { z } from "zod"` resolved to zod's `.cjs` entry (since `require` was checked before `import`), then the loader rejected it with "Cannot import a CommonJS module from ESM". Real-world impact: many modern packages with `exports: { ".": { import: ..., require: ... } }` (zod, anthropic-sdk, etc.) couldn't be ESM-imported. Fix: split into context-specific orders — ESM uses `["dun", "node", "import", "module", "require", "default"]`, CJS uses `["dun", "node", "require", "import", "module", "default"]`. `findNodeModule` threads `bool esm` through `resolveExports`/`resolveExportTarget`. Loader.d passes `esm=true` when called from the ESM module loader callback | **Done** |
| 61b | `module` condition support for legacy ESM packages | Some packages (e.g. `@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions`) declare `exports: { ".": { module, esnext, types, default } }` with NO `import` condition. Node treats `module` as an ESM-context fallback. Added `module` to both ESM and CJS condition lists (after `import`/`require` respectively) so these legacy packages resolve correctly when imported from ESM | **Done** |
| 61c | New built-in: `dun:dns/promises` (Node.js compat) | `import dnsP from 'node:dns/promises'` previously threw "Cannot find module" — the package existed as a sub-object (`require('dns').promises`) but wasn't exposed as a top-level builtin. Added: (a) `dns/promises` to `isBareBuiltin` list, (b) `dnsPromisesModuleInit` QJS C-module registration with `lookup`/`resolve4`/`resolve6`/`resolve` named exports + default, (c) `__dun_cjs_dns_promises__` global setup in dnsExtensionSource, (d) `require('dns/promises')` → `dun:dns/promises` mapping in require.d. Both `require('dns/promises').lookup(...)` and `import dns from 'node:dns/promises'` now work | **Done** |
| 61d | New permanent fixture: `dns_promises.js` | 6 checks: `require('dns/promises')` is an object, has `.lookup`/`.resolve4`, `.lookup(host)` returns a Promise, result has `.address` + `.family` (or graceful catch for sandboxed envs). Needs `--allow-net` for the actual lookup | **Done** |

| 62a | `@mustuse` on `PromiseHandles` | DIP 1038 — `engine.newPromise()` returns 3 owned JSHandles (promise + resolve + reject). Dropping the struct leaks all 3 (3 leaked `JSValueProtect` slots per drop on JSC). Adding `@mustuse` forces the compiler to flag any caller that ignores the return. Audited the 3 existing call sites (`deno_compat.d`) — all already store + use. The annotation is defensive: catches the next bug. Note: D reserves `@mustuse` on **functions** (not structs) for future use, so we can't apply the same to `Permission.check` / `checkPerm` — those rely on review + grep | **Done** |

| 63a | **CVE-2024-34346 / GHSA-23rx-c3g5-hv9w class** — privileged-path sandbox bypass | Global `--allow-read`/`--allow-write` silently granted access to `/proc/self/environ` (env-var leak), `/proc/self/maps` (ASLR layout), `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/hostname`, `/dev/*`, `/sys/*`. Reading `/proc/self/environ` escalates `--allow-read` to `--allow-env`; writing `/proc/self/mem` escalates to `--allow-all`. Reproduced on all 3 backends. Fix: `Permission.check` consults new `isPrivilegedPath(canonical)` predicate after canonicalization. For `read`/`write`, the global grant short-circuit is bypassed when the canonical resource matches `/proc/* /sys/* /dev/* /etc/*` (POSIX) or `\\?\* \\.\*` (Windows). Scoped grants and `--allow-all` still work. New permanent fixture `cve_priv_files.js` (8/8 on each backend). Verified DunJS is NOT vulnerable to CVE-2026-32260/27190 (Deno shell-metachar — already blocked by `hasShellMetaChars`) or CVE-2026-0821/0822/1145 (QuickJS-NG heap overflows ≤ 0.11.0 — DunJS bundles 0.14.0 with the upstream fixes) | **Done** |
| 63b | **`bufferConcatFused` V8 shim primitive** | `Buffer.concat([a, b])` on V8 was 3000-3500ns/op (14× slower than Node's ~220ns). Root cause: per-element FFI scope entries — for a 2-element concat that's ~11 `withContext` setups. New `dun_v8_buffer_concat(arrayHandle, count, total_len, proto)` does the whole op in ONE withContext block against v8::Local<TypedArray> directly: array walk, ByteLength sum, ArrayBuffer::New + memcpy each backing store + Uint8Array::New + SetPrototype. `IJSEngine.bufferConcatFused` virtual method; QuickJS/JSC return `JSHandle.init` to skip the fast path (their FFI overhead profile doesn't reward fusing). `jsBufferConcat` tries the fused path BEFORE the D size pass. Isolated micro-bench: 3200 → 1500ns (2.1× faster). feature_bench aggregate: dun-v8 par with Node within run-to-run noise (~158M vs ~162M ops/sec) | **Done** |
| 63c | **PGO fix**: `--whole-archive` wrap on `libldc_rt.profile` | `release-pgo-gen` build type was broken since landing — `dub build -c v8 -b release-pgo-gen` produced binaries that ran but wrote no `.profraw`. Root cause: LDC 1.42's internal linker (LLD) pulls in only `__llvm_profile_instrument_target` from the static archive (the one symbol referenced by compile-time instrumentation), missing the other 47 runtime symbols (registry, filename, begin/end markers). Fix: lflags-posix wraps the lib in `--whole-archive` / `--no-whole-archive`. After: `nm build/dun \| grep __llvm_profile_` yields 48 symbols; profraw written on every exit; `ldc-profdata merge` produces a valid 1.2 MB profile that `release-pgo` consumes. PGO impact on feature_bench was within noise (FFI-bound workload, little D branch-prediction opportunity); infrastructure now correct for future profile-targeted work | **Done** |
